newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany minister still sees jobs goal within reach.
newsitem.headline: Germany minister still sees jobs goal within reach.

text.p: German labour minister Norbert Bluem expects that the government can still reach a target of cutting unemployment by half by the year 2000, the magazine Spiegel said on Sunday.
Spiegel will say in its Monday edition, released in advance, that the ambitious jobs goal could be reached if all sectors of the economy worked together to create employment.
Germany, which has seen unemployment swell to near-record highs, hopes to reduce the number of unemployed to two million by the year 2000.

Bluem said companies had complained that regulations governing dismissals, store hours and sick pay had hindered their ability to create jobs. Now that rules are being relaxed, the burden of proof is on industry, he said.
But Hans-Olaf Henkel, president of the BDI Federation of German Industry, rejected any suggestion that companies were not creating enough jobs in an interview with the news magazine Focus.
"If companies expect to make a profit, they will hire people," Henkel told the publicication.
Henkel criticized the government for not doing more to reduce social insurance contributions as it had promised to.
Meanwhile, the German white-collar union, DAG, warned on Sunday of a possible collapse in state-sponsored job creation and training schemes.
DAG president Roland Issen said that savings proposed in these areas could force up unemployment and cold-heartedly leave the jobless "to their fate".
